limitations: Synthetic paused Chromium native touch emulation with software WebGL; not a physical phone test.
Each capture releases contacts and may pause. Automatic live ~3s / FIRE ~1.2s observation boundaries constrain play and break holds.
Pauses clear AIM and close TOOLS. No human reaction-time or causal game-quality benefit inferred.
Physical phones, Safari, audio, hardware performance and continuous enjoyment unassessed.

scores.scale: 0 unusable, 5 mixed with substantial friction, 7 good with noticeable limitations, 9 excellent across assessed use, 10 exceptional. Subjective holistic assessment of observed emulated mobile use, not a win/loss grade or hardware certification.

controls.reason: Two-contact move/fire drags and scene turns produced visible results; patrol coverage in both attempts. Tap aiming and large anchors helped. Precision and sustained rearming comfort remain uncertain because of default assists and capture releases.

gameplay.reason: Recoveries, patrol cues, coil phases and uplink created a coherent short objective sequence. Most travel was assisted and uplink completed while standing under fire; tactical depth and continuous enjoyment are not established.

presentation.reason: Cohesive rain-soaked industrial scene, teal/amber language, readable weapon silhouette, clear target-down and coil feedback. Dark structural silhouettes can merge; no audio assessment.

usability.reason: Contextual hold button, objective checkmarks, paused planning map, clear fresh-start result panel and useful route/threat cues. Brief wall-facing route views and offscreen orientation add friction.

readability.reason: Primary objective, health, ammo and large action buttons readable at 390x844. Small world signage, thin secondary lettering and dense upper status region require closer inspection.

helpful_moments: First simultaneous move/fire downed guard with clear confirmation.
Turning toward patrol revealed visibly charging sentinel, then manual combat downed it.
Map showed a short Custodian approach; closed visibly before continuing.
Each recovery changed the objective and checkmarks; coil OFF feedback made progress explicit.
frustrating_moments: Travel assist temporarily presented a close wall rather than destination.
Small world sign text is harder to read than HUD.
Offscreen threat labels require orientation; source positions cannot be inferred from labels alone.
holistic_observations.failures: No terminal losses, tooling failures, checkpoint retries or confirmed shot misses observed. No claims about actions not performed.
uncertainties: Accuracy is game-reported and includes assistance.
Short near-center FIRE drags do not establish broad aiming range or physical ergonomics.
No causal inference from paused observation frequency; no claim of human reaction time.
Unopened memories and other content not assessed for enjoyment.

protocol.read_scope: Only helper --help read for instructions; visible helper output and own captures. No game source, tests, docs, prior reviews, recordings, internal state or target metadata inspected.
protocol.input: JSON-lines native two-contact touch only. Every adaptive continuation followed a separately viewed fresh screenshot. At most one new scene target per batch; no keyboard/mouse/evaluation.
protocol.boundaries: Requested waits 900, 1100, 1500 or 3000ms, all <=12000ms. ~3s live boundaries shortened route waits; inspected output timings and new screenshots before each continuation. No bypass.
protocol.capture: Default release then live capture and pause; no captureHeld. Both capture modes would break holds. Software transport can progress between UI snapshot and screenshot (e.g. attempt1-uplink2 UI 87%, image 89%).
protocol.planning: Attempt1 map remained planning until explicit #close-map.
protocol.identity: Menu visibly BUILD 124; frozen source hash supplied by user, not independently checked under visible-only scope.
